2. What is the primary objective of optimal foraging theory?

answers.b: To maximize the net energy gained per unit time

questions.question: 3. According to the theory, a searching predator differs from a sit-and-wait predator because it:

answers.a: Waits at a fixed location for prey to approach
answers.b: Moves throughout its habitat to locate prey.

questions.question: 4. In the simulator, the handling time parameters (hp₁ and hp₂) represent:

answers.a: The time required to locate prey
answers.b: The reproductive time of the prey population
answers.c: The travel time between hunting locations
answers.d: The time required to capture and consume the prey

questions.question: 5. The overall objective of the searching predator model is to identify the strategy that:

answers.a: Minimizes predator movement regardless of energy gain
answers.b: Maximizes the number of prey captured per day
answers.c: Maximizes net energy gain by balancing prey energy content, search costs, and handling costs
answers.d: Eliminates one prey species from the ecosystem
